issues.description: torch.cuda.set_device crashes when local_rank is None default
issues.detail: In train.py main, args.local_rank defaults to None but is passed directly to torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank) before any validation. If the launcher does not set --local_rank (or sets it via env var like LOCAL_RANK), this raises TypeError immediately. Should fall back to env var LOCAL_RANK or assert/parse before use.

issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps but code reads max_step
issues.detail: DeepSpeedTrainer docstring documents max_steps/val_interval keys, but __init__ reads trainer_args["max_step"], "save_interval", "log_interval" — and val_interval is never read. Users following the docstring will hit KeyError on max_step. Reconcile keys and document/use val_interval consistently with run()/valid() cadence.

issues.description: Validation cadence ignores val_interval; runs every save_interval
issues.detail: run() calls self.train() (which advances save_interval steps) then self.valid() then save, ignoring any separate validation cadence. The documented val_interval has no effect, and validation is forced to align with saves. This silently violates the configured behavior and wastes compute when val_interval > save_interval.

issues.description: log_interval is unused; every step is logged to wandb
issues.detail: trainer_args["log_interval"] is stored but never referenced in train(); wandb.log fires every step, plus an all_reduce on stats every step which adds collective overhead. For large clusters this is a real perf and storage hit. Gate logging and all_reduce on (global_step % log_interval == 0).

issues.description: Resume loads latest checkpoint from output_dir without explicit opt-in
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint silently picks the highest step_* directory under output_dir/checkpoints whenever resume_path is unset. Re-running a job that wrote a partial/corrupt checkpoint will resume from it without the user asking. Also unsafe if checkpoint dir name parsing fails (int() will raise) on any unexpected dir. Require explicit --resume flag or guard the sort.

issues.description: valid-* specifier parsing uses split() which breaks multi-token specifiers
issues.detail: args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() splits on whitespace, but specifier format is colon-delimited 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' and likely contains no whitespace separating multiple specs (and paths may contain spaces). Multiple validation sets can't be passed reliably. Define a clear separator (e.g., comma or nargs='+') and document it; train specifier has the same ambiguity but isn't even split.

review.summary: The DeepSpeed trainer scaffolding is reasonable but has several concrete bugs and contract mismatches. The most pressing is that local_rank defaults to None and is passed straight to torch.cuda.set_device, plus the docstring/key mismatch between max_steps/val_interval and the actual max_step/save_interval keys used at runtime. Validation cadence and log_interval are not honored, resume silently auto-picks the latest checkpoint, and multi-specifier parsing via str.split() is brittle. These should be tightened before merge.
